_comment: Watchlist for the daily source check (tools/law-watch.mjs).
These are the PRIMARY statute pages behind the rules Amparo prints.
The job does NOT re-verify the law — no script can do that. It detects when
a source page's text CHANGES, which is the signal that a human needs to
re-read it. 'anchor' is a string that must appear in the page; the hash is
taken from a window around it so page furniture (ads, timestamps, nav)
URLs must point at CURRENT law, never a year-pinned snapshot (e.g. /codes/texas/2023/...) — a frozen year can never change, which would silently defeat the whole purpose of this watch.

HOST CHOICE IS ABOUT DATACENTER IPs, not content. Probed from a real GitHub Actions runner: FindLaw and Justia 403 it every time (they answer a residential IP fine, which is why local runs mislead). public.law serves the runner reliably, so TX and NY use it. Georgia stays on FindLaw because public.law has no Georgia subdomain and every other GA source tested (lawserver, onecle, elaws, casetext, legis.ga.gov) 404s, 503s or returns a JS shell. GA therefore reports 'unreachable' from CI and is only really checked on a local run — which the honest-failure handling in law-watch.mjs covers: lastChecked only advances when at least one source was actually reached.
